prompt: Evaluate: "Cost-push inflation is worse for the economy than demand-pull inflation because it simultaneously harms output while raising prices, whereas demand-pull inflation at least comes with rising output." Assess this claim using MOD-2.H.

Cost-push inflation (negative SRAS shock): PL rises AND output/employment falls simultaneously — the economy suffers both higher prices (eroding purchasing power) AND lower output (economic contraction). Demand-pull inflation (positive AD shock): PL rises but output/employment also rise — the economy grows, though with inflationary side effects. The MOD-2.H.2 asymmetry is the key: stagflation from cost-push is a double harm.

options.label: C
